# Oya Factory: full description

> Oya Factory is for AI-native teams that want to ship 100x faster and still keep the SDLC: a built-in team of agents around Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and OpenCode, your checks on every turn, any turn rewindable. Free and open source for macOS and Windows.

Website: https://oyafactory.com/
Download: https://github.com/OyadotAI/keel-releases/releases/latest
Source: https://github.com/OyadotAI/keel (MIT licence)
Made by: Oya (https://oya.dev)

## In one line

It's 2026. Still shipping with one agent?

Oya Factory puts a full agent team on every task, so you ship 100× faster and keep your SDLC.

Used by engineers from Oya, Google, Amazon, Salesforce, Jumper Media and other companies.

## The story of one feature

### Before: One agent. One terminal. You, watching.

You prompt. You wait. You approve. You check.

### The ask: You type one sentence.

Pick an agent. It starts on its own branch.

### The team: A team picks it up.

Scoped, designed, planned, built, reviewed, tested, secured.

### The lanes: Three agents. Zero collisions.

One branch each. Never the same files.

### The proof: Proof, not promises.

Your checks after every turn. Undo any turn.

### The memory: Nothing gets forgotten.

Notes travel with the task, agent to agent.

### Shipped: Shipped before lunch.

One pull request, with everything that passed.

## The platform

### A fraction of the size

A native app, not a bundled Chromium.

### Skills and plugins, handled

Recommended, installed, kept current.

### Every project, one window

All your repositories, side by side.

### Agentic mode

Agents work, you steer.

### Coding mode

An editor, the agent beside you.

## Compared with running an agent in a terminal

| | Oya Factory | An agent in a terminal |
|---|---|---|
| A branch per task | Automatic | By hand |
| Checks after every turn | Automatic | If you remember |
| Undo a turn | One click | git reflog |
| Several agents at once | Never the same files | One shared checkout |
| All four agents | One window | One CLI each |

## Frequently asked questions

### What is Oya Factory?

Oya Factory is a free, open-source desktop app for running AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and OpenCode) on your own repositories. Each task runs in its own git branch and worktree, and every diff, command, approval and check result is shown as it happens.

### Which coding agents does it support?

Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Google Antigravity and OpenCode. Oya Factory drives the agent CLIs you already have installed and signed in, so it uses your existing subscriptions.

### Is Oya Factory free?

Yes. It is MIT licensed, with no account, no license key and no limit on agent steps.

### Which platforms does it run on?

macOS and Windows.

### Does Oya Factory send my code anywhere?

Oya Factory runs on your machine and has no server of its own in between. Your agents talk to their own providers exactly as they do in a terminal.

### How is it different from running an agent in a terminal?

A terminal shows text. Oya Factory gives every task its own branch, runs your project's checks after each turn, checkpoints every turn so it can be rewound, turns permission prompts into questions in the conversation, and lets several agents work at once without sharing a working tree.

### Do I have to change my repository?

No. It works on any git repository. It can optionally add an agent team, recommended skills and a readiness scan, which it keeps current.

### How does it compare to Orca or Conductor?

See the side-by-side pages for Orca and Conductor. In short: Oya Factory focuses on proving each turn (checks, rewind, clean branches) on macOS and Windows; Orca adds remote hosts and a phone app; Conductor is a polished Mac-only app.

## Oya Factory vs Orca

Orca runs agents.Oya Factory proves their work.

Running several agents in parallel worktrees is table stakes. The hard part is trusting what they wrote. Oya Factory is built around that: every turn checked, every turn reversible, every agent kept out of the others' way.

### Your checks run on every turn

After each turn, Oya Factory runs your project's own checks and puts the verdict beside the reply. A turn that fails is never committed for you. Orca leaves verifying a turn to you.

### Any turn can be rewound

A snapshot is taken before every turn, so a bad one is undone in a click, and the undo can be undone. No digging through git history.

### Two agents never share a working tree

The daemon refuses a second writer on the same checkout, across lanes and windows, so parallel agents can't sweep up each other's half-written files.

### Projects configured for you

A readiness scan, an agent team and the skills your stack needs, added and kept current automatically.

### Lighter on your machine

Oya Factory uses the webview your operating system already has, with a small Rust daemon per project. Orca is built on Electron, which ships its own copy of Chromium.

| | Oya Factory | Orca |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | MIT | MIT |
| Price | Free | Free |
| App shell | Tauri, your OS's webview | Electron, bundled Chromium |
| Checks verdict on every turn | Built in | Not stated |
| Rewind any turn | Built in | Not stated |
| One writer per working tree | Enforced | Not stated |
| Automatic project setup | Built in | Not stated |

Orca details are from orca.dev and its documentation as of 23 November 2026; “Not stated” means its documentation does not describe the feature.

Page: https://oyafactory.com/compare/orca/

## Oya Factory vs Conductor

Conductor is a Mac app.Oya Factory is yours, everywhere.

Conductor made parallel agents feel polished on a Mac. Oya Factory brings the same workflow to macOS and Windows, open source and free, and adds proof: your checks on every turn, and agents that never collide.

### macOS and Windows

One app, one workflow, on both platforms. Conductor is macOS only.

### Free and open source

MIT licensed, no account and no paid tier. Read the code, change it, ship it.

### Your checks run on every turn

After each turn, Oya Factory runs your project's own checks and records the verdict beside the reply. A turn that fails is never committed for you.

### Your code stays on your machine

Everything runs locally; there is no cloud workspace and no server of ours between you and your repository.

### Projects configured for you

A readiness scan, an agent team and the skills your stack needs, added and kept current automatically.

| | Oya Factory | Conductor |
|---|---|---|
| Platforms | macOS and Windows | macOS |
| Licence | Open source, MIT | Not stated |
| Price | Free | Paid Pro plan |
| Runs entirely on your machine | Yes | Also offers cloud workspaces |
| Checks verdict on every turn | Built in | Not stated |
| One writer per working tree | Enforced | Not stated |

Conductor details are from conductor.build and its documentation as of 23 November 2026; “Not stated” means its site does not say.

Page: https://oyafactory.com/compare/conductor/
